title: SLI probe portfolios and span anchoring playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook for assembling a small portfolio of SLI probes tied to trace anchors and dashboard panels. Target: give product/ops/eng quick, actionable visibility into regressions for inference-serving (latency, cold starts, KV warmth, fallback rates) with constrained query budgets.

Audience:
- Observability engineers curating dashboards
- Oncall SREs who need fast triage scaffolds
- Serving/runtime owners (model and infra teams) planning rollouts

High-level approach (summary):
1) Define a small probe portfolio that covers: user-perceived latency, token-generation path latency, KV cache health, model fallback and quality regressions.
2) Anchor each probe to 1–2 trace span names and 2 metrics (one aggregate, one percentile heat).
3) Build a microdash with 6 panels per runbook: probe metric, trace-rate, top causes table, recent traces sample, cohort breakdown, and cost-impact snippet.

Suggested probe portfolio (minimal):
- user_ttf_token_probe:
  - intent: detect perceivable latency regressions for interactive flows
  - metric: ttf_token_ms_p95 (ms)
  - trace anchor spans: request_span -> generation_span
  - sampling: 100% traces on ttf_token_ms > 1000ms, 2% baseline otherwise
  - alert heuristic: p95 increases by 25% week-over-week and sustained > 800ms

- kv_warmth_probe:
  - intent: detect cold-cache-induced tail latency and cost spikes
  - metrics: kv_cache_warmth_index (0..1), kv_hit_rate_p90 (%)
  - trace anchor spans: kv_lookup_span, kv_eviction_span (if present)
  - query cadence: 5m probe, hourly aggregate
  - alert heuristic: kv_warmth_index drops > 30% or sustained kv_hit_rate_p90 < 70% for 30m

- batch_queue_probe:
  - intent: expose queuing pressure that increases p99 gen latency
  - metrics: batch_queue_time_ms_p99, batch_size_p50
  - trace anchor spans: batch_enqueue_span, batch_dequeue_span, routing_span
  - alert: p99 queue time > 25ms with sustained throughput > baseline

- fallback_and_variant_probe:
  - intent: surface increased fallbacks to smaller/legacy models or sync-to-worker failures
  - metrics: fallback_rate (count/req), fallback_latency_ratio
  - trace anchor spans: routing_span, fallback_span, model_swap_span
  - alert: fallback_rate > 0.5% for > 15 minutes on critical tenant

Metric definitions (short catalog) - keep names short, units, cardinality guidance:
- ttf_token_ms_p50/p90/p95/p99: Time from request acceptance to first non-empty token flush. unit=ms; cardinality: low (by model, region, route). retention: 30d high-resolution, 90d rollup.
- generation_latency_ms_p50/p90/p99: end-to-end generation (incl. batching). unit=ms; cardinality: model_version, tenant_id (low-card), region.
- kv_cache_warmth_index: fraction of time the prefix cache returned a KV hit before first model call; unit=0..1; cardinality: model_id, region.
- kv_hit_rate_p90: percentile of KV hit rate across sessions; unit=%; cardinality: model, route.
- batch_queue_time_ms_p99: time waiting in batch queue; unit=ms; cardinality: pool_id, model.
- fallback_rate: ratio of requests rerouted to fallback model/engine; unit=ratio; cardinality: route, tenant.
- token_cost_usd_estimate: estimated incremental token cost per minute window; unit=USD; cardinality: tenant, model.
- trace_sample_rate_effective: derived metric for debug panels showing what fraction of requests produce a stored trace.

Span design and trace anchoring recommendations:
- Standardize span names across stacks: request_span, routing_span, batch_enqueue_span, kv_lookup_span, model_infer_span, stream_flush_span, fallback_span.
- Minimal attributes to attach to spans: request_id, route, model_version, tenant_id (low-card), pool_id, sequence_length_bucket (short/medium/long). Keep any high-cardinal attributes out of tag indices.
- Span durations: record both start/end and intermediate child durations for KV lookup and model kernel time.
- Anchor probes to spans: each SLI should point to the span most likely to surface the causal bottleneck (eg. kv_probe -> kv_lookup_span).

Sampling policy (practical):
- Default: 1% baseline sampling for success paths, 100% for errors (status != OK).
- Dynamic sampling knobs:
  - increase to 10% during model rollouts (flagged by rollout_tag)
  - always sample 100% of requests with ttf_token_ms > 750ms or generation_latency_ms_p99 threshold breaches
  - tenant-weighted sampling: customers above billing threshold get boosted trace sampling (useful for dedicated capacity debugging)
- Retention tiers: full traces kept 7d for sampled baseline, 30d for error traces, 90d for critical tenants or legal hold.

Dashboard layout and panel recipes (6-panel microdash):
1) Probe summary smalltable (current value, short-term trend arrow, alert status)
   - query hint: SELECT probe_name, p95_value, delta_1h, alert_state FROM metrics.probes WHERE probe_name IN (...)
2) Heatmap: ttf_token_ms across tenant cohorts and time-of-day (bucketed by sequence_length)
   - panel: time heatmap, quantile shading, annotate deploy events
3) Trace-rate and sampling view
   - plot: traces_per_min, effective_sample_rate, error_traces_per_min
4) Top causes table (by attribution score)
   - rows: top 10 routes or pool_ids with highest p99 latency contributors (kv miss, batch queue, fallback)
5) Recent traces sample (linked trace list with small excerpt)
   - show 5 latest error or slow traces, link to full trace view
6) Cost & capacity snippet
   - small bar: token_cost_usd_estimate by tenant or model for last 1h; helps correlate cost regressions with kv misses/cold starts

Runbook checklist for investigating a probe alert (quick triage):
- Confirm alert scope (tenant/global/route) and time window
- Check recent deploys/rollouts and canary flags (linked tag)
- Open microdash and inspect top causes table
- Fetch 3 representative traces (one at p95, one error, one typical)
- If kv_warmth issue: check KV eviction logs, recent model cache invalidations, replica restarts, burst patterns
- If batch_queue issue: validate recent throughput spikes, autoscaling events, node-level CPU/GPU pressure
- If fallback increase: inspect routing config, model health endpoints, and model-size mismatch errors

KV warm/cold startup probe specifics (practical heuristics):
- Measure KV warm-up on first request of session vs nth request: define warmness = hits_on_first_10_requests / total_first_10_requests. Use session_id with bounded cardinality (session window 30m)
- Pragmatic thresholds: cold session warmness < 0.2 => aggressive prefetch candidate; warmness > 0.8 => healthy
- Pre-warm probe: synthetic background probe per pool that requests small synthetic prefixes once per 2m; track delta in generation p99 when pre-warm present vs absent

Dashboard cost/query budgeting notes:
- Favor compact quantile panels (p50/p90/p99) over heavy histograms; histograms only for deep-dive drilldowns.
- Avoid session_id cardinality in primary queries; use aggregated session buckets.
- Cache frequently used queries as materialized views where the cost justifies it (eg. kv_warmth hourly view).

Operational guardrails and ownership:
- Metric ownership: each metric must have an owner alias and contributor list. Add metric contract doc link in metric metadata.
- Dashboard ownership: microdash -> owner team + 2 backup reviewers. Keep oncall playbook link visible on panel.
- Change process: any metric name or tag change requires a three-week deprecation window with aliasing.

Open questions / decision items:
- Do we want per-tenant full-trace retention for any tier by default? (cost vs debug value)
- Standardization: enforce a single event for 'first token flush' across SDKs and gateways (client vs server).
- Do we capture token-level traces (very high-cardinality) or only span-level with derived token metrics? Proposal: Do not store raw token streams; derive token-level metrics server-side and attach aggregates to spans.

Next steps (short):
- Owner (Ava) will pilot microdash and probe for two candidate routes: interactive chat and long-form generation (ETA 2 weeks).
- Priya to prototype pre-warm synthetic probe (experiment) and publish results to linked_confluence page (ETA 3 weeks).
- Liam to add span-name enforcement to instrumentation linter and open PR for attribute whitelist.

Notes to self / rough todos (workshop style):
- Bake small SQL for kv_warmth materialized view (pseudocode in confluence link).
- Draft onboarding checklist for new model teams: include sample dashboards and how to request increased trace sampling.
- Keep this doc short and iterate; push canonical metric definitions to metrics catalog once finalized.

References and quick links:
- OBS-412 (investigate KV pre-warm probes), Confluence Probe Index, GitHub PR-789 (sampling change)
summary: Compact playbook for probe-oriented SLIs, trace anchoring, microdash layout, and operational runbook for KV warmth, cold starts, queueing, and fallbacks
